companies.name: Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria
companies.description: The Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria was founded by the Nigerian government in 1977 to replace the Nigerian Building Society. It was the only mortgage institution in Nigeria between 1978 and 1985 and was established to meet the housing needs of all Nigerian citizens.

companies.name: C&I Leasing Group PLC
companies.description: C&I Leasing Group PLC is a Nigerian public limited maritime company formed in 1990 and listed on the Nigerian stock exchange since 1997. It operates through three business units: fleet management, outsourcing, and marine vessel operations.

companies.name: Ruparelia Group
companies.description: The Ruparelia Group is a privately owned conglomerate in Uganda. It is commonly referred to as the Ruparelia Group and has Sudhir Ruparelia as a shareholder in each of its companies.

companies.name: Uganda Securities Exchange
companies.description: The Uganda Securities Exchange (USE) is the principal stock exchange of Uganda, founded in June 1997. It operates under the jurisdiction of Uganda's Capital Markets Authority, which reports to the Bank of Uganda, the country's central bank.

companies.name: East African Development Bank
companies.description: The East African Development Bank (EADB) is a regional development finance institution located in Kampala, Uganda. It promotes development in East African Community member countries including Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, and Tanzania, and has been operating since its charter was developed after its initiation in 1967.

companies.name: Bank of Africa
companies.description: Bank of Africa Uganda Limited (BOA Uganda) is a commercial bank licensed by the Bank of Uganda, the country's central bank and banking regulator.

companies.name: Centenary Bank Uganda
companies.description: Centenary Bank, also known as Centenary Rural Development Bank Limited, is a commercial bank in Uganda. It is licensed by the Bank of Uganda, the country's central bank and national banking regulator. The bank operates within Uganda's financial services sector.

companies.name: DFCU Group
companies.description: The Development Finance Company of Uganda Group, or DFCU Group, operates in both the financial and real estate sectors in Uganda. It is a notable company within Uganda's financial services industry.

companies.name: Orient Bank
companies.description: Orient Bank, now known as I&M Bank (Uganda) Limited, is a commercial bank licensed by the Bank of Uganda. It was rebranded after I&M Bank acquired 90 percent shareholding in Orient Bank. The bank operates in Uganda's financial services sector.

companies.name: Stanbic Bank Uganda Limited
companies.description: Stanbic Bank Uganda Limited is a commercial bank licensed by the Bank of Uganda, the central bank and national banking regulator. It operates within Uganda's financial services sector.

companies.name: Cairo International Bank
companies.description: Cairo Bank Uganda Limited, formerly Cairo International Bank, is a commercial bank in Uganda licensed by the Bank of Uganda. It is a subsidiary of the Egypt-based Banque du Caire Group.

companies.name: Kiira Motors Corporation
companies.description: Kiira Motors Corporation is a state-owned automotive manufacturer in Uganda established to develop the country's automotive industry and commercialize the Kiira Electric Vehicle Project. The government holds the majority equity, with Makerere University as a minority partner.

companies.name: Nile Breweries Limited
companies.description: Nile Breweries Limited is the leading beer manufacturer in Uganda. It operates within the brewing industry in the country.

companies.name: MTN Uganda
companies.description: MTN Uganda is the largest telecommunications company in Uganda, holding a significant market share of mobile subscribers. It operates within Uganda's telecommunications industry.

companies.name: Embassy of France, Kampala
companies.description: The Embassy of France in Uganda is the diplomatic mission of France located in Kampala, Uganda's capital. Since 2022, its ambassador has been Xavier Sticker.

companies.name: Refugee Law Project
companies.description: The Refugee Law Project is a human rights NGO established in 1999 as an outreach project of Makerere University's School of Law. It focuses on addressing refugee rights in Uganda.

companies.name: Tororo Cement Limited
companies.description: Tororo Cement Limited (TCL) is a Ugandan company and one of the largest manufacturers of construction materials in East Africa. It is based in Uganda and specializes in producing cement and related building materials.

companies.name: Wakaliwood
companies.description: Wakaliwood, also known as Ramon Film Productions, is a film studio located in Wakaliga, a slum in Kampala, Uganda. It is known for producing ultra-low budget action movies, including titles like Who Killed Captain Alex? and Bad Black.

companies.name: Eagle Air
companies.description: Eagle Air is an airline based in Kampala, Uganda, operating regional scheduled services and charter flights across East and Central Africa. Its main base is Entebbe International Airport, with a second hub at Arua Airport in Northern Uganda.

companies.name: Royal Daisy Airlines
companies.description: Royal Daisy Airlines was a private airline in Uganda that is no longer in business. It operated in the aviation sector within Uganda before ceasing operations.

companies.name: BAR Aviation Uganda
companies.description: BAR Aviation Uganda is an aviation company based in Uganda offering charter services, pilot training, air ambulance services, and aircraft maintenance. Its main base is Entebbe International Airport, with a second hub at Kajjansi Airport in Wakiso District.

companies.name: Rwandatel
companies.description: Rwandatel was a telephony company headquartered in Kigali, Rwanda. It operated in the telecommunications sector providing telephony services in Rwanda.

companies.name: Banque Populaire du Rwanda
companies.description: BPR Bank Rwanda, formerly Banque Populaire du Rwanda SA, is a commercial bank licensed by the National Bank of Rwanda. It operates in Rwanda's financial services sector providing banking services.

companies.name: Bralirwa
companies.description: Bralirwa, also known as Brasseries et Limonaderies du Rwanda, is the largest brewer and soft beverage company in Rwanda. It is publicly traded on the Rwanda Stock Exchange and produces a variety of beverages.

companies.name: Fina Bank
companies.description: Guaranty Trust Bank (Rwanda) plc, commonly known as GTBank Rwanda, is a licensed commercial bank in Rwanda. It has been part of the Nigerian Guaranty Trust Bank since 2013, operating in the financial services sector.

companies.name: RwandAir
companies.description: RwandAir Limited is the national flag carrier airline of Rwanda, headquartered in Kigali. It operates flights to 25 destinations across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia from its primary hub at Kigali International Airport.

companies.name: STP Airways
companies.description: STP Airways is the national airline of São Tomé and Príncipe. It is banned from operating into the European Union, so its flights are operated by the Portuguese airline EuroAtlantic Airways. The airline is based in São Tomé and Príncipe.

companies.name: Banco Internacional de São Tomé e Príncipe
companies.wiki: Banco Internacional de São Tomé e Príncipe
companies.logo_file: Banco Internacional de São Tomé e Príncipe Logo.jpg
companies.description: Banco Internacional de São Tomé e Príncipe (BISTP) is the largest and oldest commercial bank in São Tomé and Príncipe. It has a head office and 14 branches. The bank's name translates to International Bank of São Tomé and Príncipe.

companies.name: Africa's Connection STP
companies.description: Africa's Connection STP is an airline based in São Tomé. In 2014, it operated scheduled and charter services to Central and West Africa using 3 Dornier 228 aircraft. The airline is based in São Tomé and Príncipe.

companies.name: La Poste Sénégal
companies.description: La Poste Sénégal is a postal service company in Senegal. It is a member of the Universal Postal Union. The company provides mail services in Senegal.

companies.name: Bank of West Africa
companies.description: The Bank of West Africa, formerly known as Banque du Sénégal and Banque internationale pour l'Afrique occidentale (BIAO), was headquartered in Dakar. It was the main or only commercial bank and bank of issue in French Senegal and French West Africa for most of its history.

companies.name: AWA : la revue de la femme noire
companies.description: AWA : la revue de la femme noire was a Senegalese women's magazine published monthly from 1964 to 1973. It focused on topics relevant to black women in Senegal. The magazine is no longer in publication.

companies.name: Senegalese Red Cross Society
companies.description: The Senegalese Red Cross Society was established by decree in 1962. It has its headquarters in Dakar. The organization provides emergency and relief services in Senegal.

companies.name: Groupement Aérien Sénégalais
companies.description: Groupement Aérien Sénégalais is the governmental airline of Senegal based in Dakar. Its main base is Dakar-Yoff-Léopold Sédar Senghor International Airport. The airline serves the Senegalese government.

companies.name: Air Senegal
companies.description: Air Senegal is the flag carrier of the Republic of Senegal, created in 2016. It is state owned through the investment arm Caisse des Dépots et Consignation du Sénégal. The airline is based at Blaise Diagne International Airport in Dakar.

companies.name: OKX
companies.description: OKX, formerly known as OKEx, is a cryptocurrency exchange based in San Jose, California. It operates in the digital currency trading sector and has undergone a rebranding from its original name.

companies.name: Huobi
companies.description: HTX, formerly known as Huobi, is a Seychelles-based cryptocurrency exchange with offices in Hong Kong, South Korea, Japan, and the United States. Founded in China, it became a publicly listed Hong Kong company in August 2018 and is owned by cryptocurrency billionaire Justin Sun.

companies.name: Environmental Foundation for Africa
companies.description: The Environmental Foundation for Africa (EFA) is a non-governmental organization focused on protecting and restoring the environment in West Africa through community-led programs. Founded in 1992 in the UK as the Environmental Foundation for Sierra Leone, it operates locally in Sierra Leone and Liberia and is registered as a charity in England and Wales.

companies.name: Fly 6ix
companies.description: Fly 6ix was a passenger airline headquartered in Freetown, Sierra Leone. It operated flights out of Lungi International Airport before ceasing operations.

companies.name: Netco
companies.description: North Eastern Telecommunications Company is a telecommunications firm established in 1993 in Bosaso, the commercial capital of Puntland, a federal regional state of Somalia. It provides telecom services in the region.

companies.name: NationLink Telecom
companies.description: NationLink Telecom is a telecommunications company based in Somalia. It operates within the country's telecom industry.

companies.name: Golis Telecom Somalia
companies.description: Golis Telecom is the largest telecommunications operator in Puntland, northeastern Somalia. Founded in 2002, it offers GSM mobile, fixed line, and internet services, covering major cities and over 50 districts in Puntland.

companies.name: Hormuud Telecom
companies.description: Hormuud Telecom Somalia Inc. is a privately held telecommunications company based in Mogadishu. It is Somalia's largest telecom company and private-sector employer, and the first private enterprise in the country to receive international ISO certification.

companies.name: Somafone
companies.description: Somafone Telecommunications Service Company is a leading telecommunications firm in Somalia. Established in 2003 as a subsidiary of Somafone FZ LLC of Dubai Internet City, its head offices are located in Mogadishu.

companies.name: Telesom
companies.description: Telesom is a private telecommunications company founded in 2002 by local entrepreneurs in Hargeisa, Somaliland. It is the leading ICT service provider in the country, offering voice, mobile broadband, fixed broadband, SMS, mobile money, education, infotainment, and cloud services.

companies.name: Somali Telecom Group
companies.description: Somali Telecom Group (STG) is a telecommunications company founded in 1993 in Rockville, Maryland, USA. It is Somalia's first telecom service provider and maintains offices in 10 Somali cities, with its head offices currently located in Dubai.

companies.name: Arlaadi Media Network
companies.description: Arlaadi Media Network (AMN) is an independent media organization based in Somalia, launched in 2021. It is the first network in Somalia to broadcast in the Maay dialect and operates an FM radio station, a television channel, and a research arm called the Arlaadi Institute for Policy Studies.

companies.name: Somali Postal Service
companies.description: The Somali Postal Service is the national postal service of Somalia and operates under the Federal Government of Somalia's Ministry of Communications and Technology.

companies.name: International Bank of Somalia
companies.description: The International Bank of Somalia (IBS) is a bank headquartered in Mogadishu, Somalia.

companies.name: Somali National Television
companies.description: Somali National Television (SNTV) is the state media television station owned by the Federal Government of Somalia.

companies.name: Radio Garowe
companies.description: Radio Garowe is a radio station based in Garowe, Puntland, Somalia. Established in 2004, it broadcasts daily on 89.8 FM and launched an additional FM station in Bosaso in 2013.

companies.name: Puntland TV and Radio
companies.description: Puntland TV and Radio is the public broadcasting network owned by the Puntland government in Somalia. Established in 2013, it broadcasts locally and globally via satellite and shortwave, with headquarters in Garowe and an office in London.

companies.name: Jubba Airways
companies.description: Jubba Airways is a Somali airline operating domestic passenger and cargo flights within Somalia and to destinations in the Middle East.

companies.name: Air Somalia
companies.description: Air Somalia was a privately owned airline based in Somalia and was the first private airline owned entirely by Somali nationals.

companies.name: Sudanese Red Crescent Society
companies.description: The Sudanese Red Crescent is the largest humanitarian organization in Sudan, established in 1956. It operates nationwide with 15 state branches and a large volunteer network, maintaining partnerships with public authorities and international agencies.

companies.name: Sudapet
companies.description: Sudapet is a state-owned oil company based in Sudan. Founded in 1997, it is fully owned by the Ministry for Energy and Mining. The company operates in the petroleum industry within Sudan.

companies.name: Bank Balad
companies.description: Bank Balad, originally founded as Al Shamal Islamic Bank in 1983, is a major financial institution in Sudan. It rebranded to Balad Bank in 2018 and is recognized as one of the leading Islamic banks worldwide.

companies.name: Sudatel
companies.description: Sudatel is a telecommunications and Internet service provider in Sudan. It is responsible for building and maintaining the country's telecom infrastructure and is majority owned by the Sudanese government. Sudatel's stock is listed on the Bahrain Stock Exchange.

companies.name: Expresso Telecom
companies.description: Expresso Telecom is an African telecommunications company operating in Mauritania, Senegal, and Sudan. It plays a key role in the Africa Coast to Europe submarine cable project and is 75% owned by Sudatel.

companies.name: Air West
companies.description: Air West is an airline based in Khartoum, Sudan, operating domestic passenger services and international cargo charters. Its main base is Khartoum International Airport, with a hub at Sharjah International Airport.

companies.name: Sudan Airways
companies.description: Sudan Airways is the state-owned flag carrier airline of Sudan, headquartered in Khartoum. It serves as the national airline of the country.

companies.name: Mid Airlines
companies.description: Mid Airlines is a charter airline based in Khartoum, Sudan, operating domestic passenger services. Its main base is Khartoum International Airport, and it is currently banned from flying in EU airspace.

companies.name: Juba Air Cargo
companies.description: Juba Air Cargo was a cargo airline based in Khartoum, Sudan, established in 1996. It operated domestic cargo services from Khartoum International Airport before ceasing all operations in 2008.

companies.name: Tarco Aviation
companies.description: Tarco Aviation is a private airline established in 2009 in Sudan. Initially based in Khartoum, it moved operations to Port Sudan due to the 2023 Sudanese civil war.

companies.name: Sun Air
companies.description: Sun Air Aviation is a private airline based in Khartoum, Sudan, currently inoperative. It operated scheduled domestic and international flights but is banned from EU airspace as of 2021.

companies.name: Nova Airways
companies.description: Nova Airways is a passenger airline based in Khartoum, Sudan. It was formerly known as Nova Airlines from 2006 to 2011. The airline is currently banned from EU airspace.

companies.name: Swaziland Posts and Telecommunications
companies.description: Eswatini Posts and Telecommunications Corporation (EPTC) is a parastatal company in Eswatini providing postal and telecommunications services. It is divided into four units: Eswatini Post, Eswatini Telecom, Phutfumani Couriers, and National Contact Centre. The company reports to the Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology.

companies.name: Swaziland Stock Exchange
companies.description: The Eswatini Stock Exchange (ESE) is a small stock exchange headquartered in Mbabane, Eswatini. It was established in 1990 as a non-bank credit institution by Barnabas Sibusiso Dlamini, a former World Bank executive and later Prime Minister of Eswatini.

companies.name: Nairobi Stock Exchange
companies.description: The Nairobi Securities Exchange (NSE) was established in 1954 as the Nairobi Stock Exchange and is based in Nairobi, Kenya. It began as a voluntary association of stockbrokers registered under the Societies Act in British Kenya. The exchange had 66 listed companies as of February 2021.

companies.name: I&M Bank Limited
companies.description: I&M Bank Kenya Limited is a commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Kenya, the national banking regulator. It operates in Kenya, the largest economy in the East African Community.

companies.name: Hass Petroleum
companies.description: HASS Petroleum is a privately owned oil marketing company headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya. It operates in the petroleum industry within the country.

companies.name: Kenya Electricity Generating Company
companies.description: Kenya Electricity Generating Company PLC (KenGen) is a government enterprise responsible for electricity production in Kenya. It is the largest electric power producer in the country, generating over 60% of the electricity consumed.

companies.name: Kenya Power and Lighting Company
companies.description: Kenya Power and Lighting Company, also known as Kenya Power or KPLC, is a public liability company that transmits, distributes, and retails electricity throughout Kenya. It operates in the electrical industry and serves customers nationwide.

companies.name: Telkom Kenya
companies.description: Telkom Kenya is an integrated telecommunications provider based in Kenya. Established in April 1999 after the split of the Kenya Posts and Telecommunications Corporation, it is fully owned by the Government of Kenya as of 2023.

companies.name: African Airlines Association
companies.description: The African Airlines Association (AFRAA) is a trade association of African airlines founded in Accra, Ghana, in 1968. As of 2021, it is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, and aims to establish and facilitate cooperation between African airlines.

companies.name: Bluebird Aviation
companies.description: Bluebird Aviation is a regional airline based in Nairobi, Kenya, established in 1992. It operates regional charter services with its main base at Wilson Airport in Nairobi.

companies.name: Fly540
companies.description: Fly540 was a low-cost airline based in Nairobi, Kenya, that commenced operations in 2006 offering passenger and cargo services. It had subsidiaries in Ghana and Angola and ceased operations in September 2022 before entering receivership in August 2026.

companies.name: Astral Aviation
companies.description: Astral Aviation is a cargo airline based in Nairobi, Kenya, established in 2000 and operating since 2001. It offers scheduled and ad-hoc cargo charters and humanitarian flights across Africa, Asia, and to Belgium, with a subsidiary in India operating since 2022.

companies.name: East African Safari Air
companies.description: East African Safari Air was a Kenyan airline whose international operations were suspended in 2004. It maintained regional and domestic services through its subsidiary East African Safari Air Express, which was purchased and rebranded as Fly SAX in 2010.

companies.name: ALS – Aircraft Leasing Services
companies.description: ALS – Aircraft Leasing Services is a regional airline based in Nairobi, Kenya. It operates within the airline industry serving regional routes.

companies.name: Safarilink Aviation
companies.description: Safarilink Aviation Limited is a regional airline based at Wilson Airport in Nairobi, Kenya. It operates regional air services within the country.

companies.name: Eastafrican.com
companies.description: Eastafrican.com, formerly East African Safari Air and Fly-SAX, is a Kenyan airline based at Wilson Airport in Nairobi. It was rebranded after being purchased by the parent company of Fly540.

companies.name: Jambojet
companies.description: Jambojet Limited is a Kenyan low-cost airline that began operations on April 1, 2014. It operates as a subsidiary of Kenya Airways and is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya. The airline focuses on providing affordable air travel within the region.

companies.name: Skyward Airlines
companies.description: Skyward Airlines is a private airline operating in Kenya, providing scheduled passenger and cargo services. Its main operational bases are Wilson Airport and Jomo Kenyatta International Airport, both located in Nairobi, Kenya's capital city.

companies.name: Commercial Bank of Ethiopia
companies.description: The Commercial Bank of Ethiopia is the largest commercial bank in Ethiopia, with a vast network of branches across the country. It employs over 35,000 people and holds a significant share of deposits and loans in Ethiopia's banking sector.

companies.name: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
companies.wiki: African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights
companies.description: The African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights is a quasi-judicial body that promotes and protects human rights across Africa. It interprets the African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights and investigates violations, although it lacks enforcement power.

companies.name: Ethiopian Red Cross Society
companies.description: The Ethiopian Red Cross Society is a humanitarian organization partnering with the Ethiopian government and international Red Cross and Red Crescent bodies. It has millions of fee-paying members and over 500,000 volunteers working in relief efforts.

companies.name: Ethiopian Airlines
companies.description: Ethiopian Airlines is the flag carrier of Ethiopia, wholly owned by the government. Founded in 1945, it began operations in 1946 and expanded to international flights in 1951. The airline became a share company in 1965 and changed its name to Ethiopian Airlines.

companies.name: Trans Nation Airways
companies.description: Trans Nation Airways is a charter airline based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Established in 2004, it is a subsidiary of the MIDROC Ethiopia Technology Group, owned by Sheikh Mohammed Hussein Al Amoudi.

companies.name: National Airways Ethiopia
companies.description: National Airways Ethiopia, formerly Air Ethiopia, is a private airline based in Addis Ababa. Established in 2007, it has been operating charter services since 2009.

companies.name: Forestry Commission of Ghana
companies.description: The Forestry Commission is a government agency in Ghana under the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources. It is responsible for forestry-related activities in the country.

companies.name: Ghana Broadcasting Corporation
companies.description: The Ghana Broadcasting Corporation was established by law in 1968 as a state, public service, and commercial broadcaster. It is headquartered in Accra, Ghana, and is funded through grants, commercials, and a television license fee.

companies.name: Ghana News Agency
companies.description: The Ghana News Agency (GNA) is a state-owned news agency in Ghana, founded in 1957 by Kwame Nkrumah. It was established with help from Reuters and served as a key source of news dissemination in Ghana and Africa. The agency was known for spreading the ideology of the African Revolution and contributing to African and Ghanaian emancipation.

companies.name: TV3 Ghana
companies.description: TV3 is a free-to-air television network based in Ghana, launched in 1997 by a Malaysian company. It produces and airs various television programs including dramas and reality shows. In 2011, it was acquired by Media General Ghana Limited.

companies.name: Accra Brewery Limited
companies.description: Accra Brewery Limited is a brewery located in Accra, Ghana. It operates in the beverage industry producing beer and related products. The company is based in Ghana's capital city.

companies.name: Enterprise Insurance
companies.description: Enterprise Group Plc is a Ghanaian insurance company incorporated in 2008. It serves as the parent company for its subsidiaries in the insurance sector. The company operates within Ghana's financial services industry.

companies.name: GCB Bank
companies.description: GCB Bank Limited, formerly Ghana Commercial Bank, is the largest bank in Ghana by total operating assets and industry deposits. It is licensed by the Bank of Ghana and absorbed deposits and assets from UT Bank and Capital Bank in 2017. The bank plays a significant role in Ghana's banking sector.

companies.name: Republic Bank Ghana Limited
companies.description: Republic Bank (Ghana) PLC is a commercial bank licensed by the Bank of Ghana. It operates as a financial institution providing banking services within Ghana. The bank is regulated by the national banking authority.

companies.name: National Investment Bank
companies.description: National Investment Bank (NIB) is a state-owned commercial bank in Ghana focused on promoting industrialization. It is licensed by the Bank of Ghana and has undergone restructuring to improve its financial standing. The bank supports various sectors of the Ghanaian economy.

companies.name: Access Bank Ghana Limited
companies.description: Access Bank Ghana Plc is a full-service commercial bank licensed by the Bank of Ghana. It provides a range of banking services within Ghana. The bank operates under the regulation of the national banking authority.

companies.name: Agricultural Development Bank of Ghana
companies.description: Agricultural Development Bank of Ghana (ADB) is a government-owned development and commercial bank. It is the first development finance institution established by the Ghanaian government, providing financial and technical services to agribusiness and rural enterprises. The bank is licensed by the Bank of Ghana.

companies.name: AnimaxFYB Studio
companies.description: AnimaxFYB Studios is an animation multimedia company based in Ghana, founded by Francis Yushua Brown. The studio specializes in 2D and 3D animation and visual effects, telling African stories through animation. It is the first African studio to have a project selected by Amazon Prime.

companies.name: Kantanka Automobile
companies.description: Kantanka Automobile is a Ghanaian automotive company that designs, manufactures, assembles, and sells luxury cars. Established in 1994 by Kwadwo Safo Kantanka, it produces vehicles using over 75% local components. The company manufactured its first SUV, the Onantefo, in 2006.

companies.name: Ghana Water Company Ltd.
companies.description: Ghana Water Limited is the sole government-owned water utility company in Ghana. It is responsible for the production, transmission, and distribution of potable water in urban areas across the country. The company was formerly known as Ghana Water Company Limited and other names.

companies.name: Ghana Red Cross Society
companies.description: The Ghana Red Cross Society is an international humanitarian organization established by an act of Parliament in 1958. It is affiliated with the International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent and has its headquarters in Accra, Ghana.

companies.name: Eco Warriors Movement
companies.description: Eco Warrior Movement is a Ghanaian non-governmental organization focused on climate change and environmental sustainability. Founded in 2020 by environmental scientist Otuo-Akyampong Boakye, it works with youth to restore degraded landscapes and mitigate climate change through an inclusive approach.

companies.name: Ghana National Petroleum Corporation
companies.description: The Ghana National Petroleum Corporation is a state agency responsible for exploration, licensing, and distribution of petroleum-related activities in Ghana. It oversees the country's petroleum industry operations.

companies.name: Total Petroleum Ghana
companies.description: TotalEnergies Marketing Ghana PLC, formerly Mobil Oil Ghana Limited, is a Ghanaian petroleum company. It operated 225 petrol stations across Ghana as of 2006 and held a significant market share. The company is listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange.

companies.name: Mr & Miss Akuapem
companies.description: Mr. & Miss Akuapem is an annual unisex beauty pageant in Ghana focused on the culture of the Akuapem people in the Eastern region. The pageant aims to promote development through culture and unity.

companies.name: Leti Arts
companies.description: Leti Arts is a Ghanaian video game company headquartered in Accra. It was founded by Eyram Tawia, who is a member of the Harambe Entrepreneur Alliance.

companies.name: Vodafone Ghana
companies.description: Vodafone Ghana, formerly Ghana Telecom, is the national telecommunications company of Ghana. In February 2024, it was fully rebranded to Telecel Ghana.

companies.name: GH One TV
companies.description: GHOne TV is a Ghana-based entertainment channel offering lifestyle, music, fashion, series, children's programs, comedy, and tourism content. Owned by Excellence In Broadcasting Networks, it is the 5th most watched TV station in Ghana.

companies.name: Asoriba
companies.description: Asoriba is a technology company headquartered in Accra, Ghana. It provides a web application for church management and a mobile app that connects churches and worshipers, including donation functionality. The company also has a presence in Nigeria, Kenya, and South Africa.

companies.name: Aerogem Aviation
companies.description: Aerogem Aviation Ltd was a Ghanaian cargo airline based in Accra, Ghana. It operated worldwide non-scheduled cargo flights with main bases at Accra International Airport and Sharjah International Airport in the UAE. Its head office was located in the Gemini Airlines Building at Accra International Airport.

companies.name: Johnsons Air
companies.description: Johnsons Air was a Ghanaian airline based at Accra International Airport, founded in 1996 by Farzin Azima. It operated ad hoc cargo services but was blacklisted in Belgium and the EU due to safety concerns before ceasing operations.

companies.name: Starbow
companies.description: Aero Surveys Limited, trading as Starbow, was a privately owned airline in Ghana operating from 2012 until 2017. It was based in Ghana during its operational years.

companies.name: Passion Air
companies.description: Pisces Aviation is a domestic airline of Ghana with its head office and main hub at Accra International Airport in Accra. It operates within Ghana.

companies.name: Terra
companies.description: Terra was a Spanish Internet multinational company owned by Telefónica, headquartered in Spain with offices in multiple countries including Brazil and the US. Founded in 1999, it operated as a web portal and Internet access provider in Spain, the US, and Latin America before becoming a wholly owned subsidiary of Telefónica in 2017.

companies.name: Adzuna
companies.description: Adzuna is a search engine specializing in job advertisements. The summary does not specify its headquarters or additional details.

companies.name: Brasil Paralelo
companies.description: Brasil Paralelo is a Brazilian media company founded in Porto Alegre and headquartered in São Paulo since 2020. It produces documentaries offering alternative viewpoints on politics, history, and current events, distributing content primarily through its subscription streaming platform and YouTube channel.

companies.name: Tecnologia Automotiva Catarinense
companies.description: Tecnologia Automotiva Catarinense (TAC) is an automotive corporation established in 2004 in Joinville, Brazil. Supported by BNDES, it opened its plant in 2008 and developed the SUV TAC Stark in collaboration with Portuguese company Datasul.

companies.name: Neiva
companies.description: Indústria Aeronáutica Neiva is a subsidiary of Embraer producing airplanes and aircraft components in Brazil. Its main product is the Embraer EMB 202 Ipanema, the most used agricultural aircraft in Brazil and the first alcohol-powered airplane.

companies.name: Puma
companies.description: Puma Automóveis Ltda. is a Brazilian sports car manufacturer established in 1963. It underwent several name changes, becoming Puma Veículos e Motores in 1964 and Puma Indústria de Veículos SA in 1974. The company is based in Brazil and specializes in automotive production.

companies.name: RBS TV
companies.description: RBS TV is a Southern Brazilian television network owned by Grupo RBS. It is one of the oldest affiliates of Rede Globo and originally stood for Rede Brasil Sul de Televisão, though it no longer uses the full name on-air. The network operates in Brazil's television industry.

companies.name: Star One
companies.description: Embratel Star One is a Brazilian communication satellite company and a subsidiary of Embratel. It operates in the telecommunications industry and is based in Brazil, providing satellite communication services.

companies.name: Vídeo Brinquedo
companies.description: Vídeo Brinquedo is a Brazilian animation studio based in São Paulo. It is known for producing animated films considered to be inexpensive mockbusters of more successful films from major studios like Walt Disney and Pixar. The company operates in the animation sector.

companies.name: GloboNews
companies.description: GloboNews is a Brazilian news-based pay television channel owned by Canais Globo, a division of Globo. It operates within Brazil's journalism and media industry, providing news content via pay TV.

companies.name: Claro Brasil
companies.description: Claro Brasil is a telecommunications operator in Brazil offering mobile, satellite television, fixed, and broadband services. It was formed in 2003 through the merger of six regional operators including Americel and ATL. The company serves the Brazilian telecommunications market.

companies.name: Synergy Group
companies.description: Synergy Group Corp. is a South American conglomerate headquartered in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, owned by Germán Efromovich. It operates airlines such as Avianca Group and is involved in oil and natural gas exploration, hydroelectric power, telecommunications infrastructure, shipbuilding, radiochemistry, agriculture, and hospitality.

companies.name: Votorantim Group
companies.description: Votorantim S.A. is a permanently capitalized investment holding company based in Brazil. It has a long-term investment approach with portfolio companies operating in 16 countries across sectors including building materials, finance, aluminum, renewable energy, metals, mining, orange juice, steel, real estate, and infrastructure.

companies.name: PinGuim Content
companies.description: PinGuim Content is a Brazilian animation studio founded in 1989 by Kiko Mistrorigo and Célia Catunda. It operates in the animation industry and is based in Brazil.

companies.name: Copa Studio
companies.description: Copa Studio is a Brazilian animation studio based in Rio de Janeiro, founded in 2009. It produces animated series such as Trunk Train and Jorel's Brother for Cartoon Network, as well as movies and television specials. The studio is known for its work in children's animation.

companies.name: Editora Abril
companies.description: Editora Abril is a major Brazilian publisher and printing company founded in 1950 by Victor Civita in São Paulo. It is one of the largest media holdings in Latin America and is part of Grupo Abril. The company operates in the mass media industry.

companies.name: Habib's
companies.description: Habib's is a Brazilian fast food company specializing in Middle Eastern cuisine and Brazilian sandwiches. It operates over 475 outlets across Brazil and has begun expanding into foreign markets. The company is known for offering Lebanese-Brazilian dishes at low prices.

companies.name: Vale Fertilizantes
companies.description: Vale Fertilizantes is a Brazilian fertilizer company founded in 2010 after Vale acquired Fosfertil. It operates in the agriculture sector, producing fertilizers for the Brazilian market. The company is a subsidiary of the mining giant Vale.

companies.name: Universo Online
companies.description: Universo Online is a Brazilian company providing web content, products, and services. It is part of the Grupo Folha enterprise. The company operates in the online service provider industry.

companies.name: Samarco
companies.description: Samarco Mineração S.A. is a Brazilian mining company founded in 1977. It is a joint venture equally owned by the Brazilian company Vale and the Australian company BHP. Samarco operates in the mining industry.

companies.name: Brazilian Development Bank
companies.description: The National Bank for Economic and Social Development (BNDES) is a Brazilian development bank structured as a federal public company linked to the Ministry of the Economy. It provides long-term financing to projects that contribute to Brazil's development. BNDES is one of the largest development banks globally.

companies.name: Clara
companies.description: Clara is a financial technology company headquartered in São Paulo, Brazil. It offers corporate credit cards, digital payment accounts, and expense management software for businesses in Latin America. Clara operates in the fintech sector.

companies.name: BIG Bompreço
companies.description: Bompreço was a chain of supermarkets and hypermarkets in Brazil, with a name meaning "good price" in Portuguese. As of 2022, Bompreço is owned by Carrefour Brazil. The company operated in the retail sector.

companies.name: Volkswagen Trucks and Buses
companies.logo_file: Logo da Volkswagen Caminhões e Ônibus.svg
companies.description: Volkswagen Truck & Bus Indústria e Comércio de Veículos Ltda. is a Brazilian commercial vehicle manufacturer based in Resende, Brazil. It is a subsidiary of Traton and produces heavy trucks and buses under the Volkswagen brand.

companies.name: Comil
companies.description: Comil Carrocerias e Onibus is a Brazilian bus and coach manufacturer established in 1985 and based in Erechim, Rio Grande do Sul. It also operates a factory in Mexico and exports products to 29 countries. The company also manufactures grain storage buildings and equipment.

companies.name: Banco BV
companies.description: Banco BV is the seventh largest bank in Brazil, founded in 1988 and headquartered in São Paulo. It operates in wholesale, retail, treasury, asset management, and brokerage sectors.

companies.name: Grupo Petrópolis
companies.description: Cervejaria Petrópolis is a Brazilian brewery headquartered in Petrópolis. It operates six industrial plants across Brazil and has operations in Germany and Paraguay.

companies.name: Volkswagen do Brasil
companies.description: Volkswagen do Brasil Ltda. is a subsidiary of Volkswagen Group established in 1953. It assembled the Volkswagen Type 1 locally and produced over 20 million vehicles in Brazil, leading the market for most of its existence.

companies.name: Chamonix
companies.description: Chamonix NG Cars is a Brazilian automobile manufacturer based in São Paulo, founded in 1981. The company was formerly located in Jarinu and was founded by Milton Masteguin and Chuck Beck.

companies.name: Obvio!
companies.description: Obvio! is a Brazilian automobile manufacturer specializing in microcars. The company planned to sell cars in the US through ZAP and was wound down after the death of designer Anísio Campos in 2019.

companies.name: Mesbla
companies.description: Mesbla S.A. was a Brazilian department store chain founded in 1912 as a subsidiary of a French firm. The company declared bankruptcy in 1999.

companies.name: Muricy
companies.description: Muricy was a Brazilian department store chain founded in 1976 and dissolved in 1998. It also operated in Chile between 1981 and 1990.

companies.name: Caemi
companies.description: Caemi Mineração e Metallurgia S.A. was a major Brazilian mining holding company that merged into Vale in 2006. The name Caemi stands for Auxiliary Company of Mining Companies.

companies.name: Giraffas
companies.description: Giraffas is a Brazilian fast-food chain founded in 1981, with its first store located in Lago Sul, Federal District. It began franchising in 1991 and has expanded across Brazil, Paraguay, and Miami in the United States.

companies.name: Koni Store
companies.description: Koni Store is a Brazilian chain of Japanese fast-food outlets headquartered in Rio de Janeiro. It offers dishes like temakis and sushi and operates 32 stores across four Brazilian states and the Federal District.

companies.name: Spoleto
companies.description: Spoleto is a Brazilian restaurant chain that applies the fast food concept to Italian cuisine. The restaurant is named after the town of Spoleto in Italy.

companies.name: Mascarello
companies.description: Mascarello Carrocerias de Ônibus is a Brazilian bus and coach manufacturer based in Cascavel, Paraná state.

companies.name: Carbuss - Indústria de Carrocerias Catarinense Ltda.
companies.description: Carbuss - Indústria de Carrocerias Catarinense Ltda. is a Brazilian bus manufacturer based in Joinville, operating on premises formerly owned by the bankrupt bus maker Busscar.

companies.name: Buscapé
companies.description: Buscapé is a Latin American comparison shopping service co-founded in São Paulo, Brazil in 1999 by Romero Rodrigues and others.

companies.name: Casas Bahia
companies.description: Casas Bahia is a Brazilian retail chain specializing in furniture and home appliances, founded in 1952 in São Caetano do Sul, São Paulo by Samuel Klein. The Klein family controls Via Varejo, which owns the store.

companies.name: Extra Mercado
companies.description: Extra Hipermercados, known as Extra, is a Brazilian hypermarket and supermarket chain owned by Grupo Pão de Açúcar.

companies.name: Casa & Video
companies.description: Casa & Vídeo is a department store chain founded in Rio de Janeiro in 1988, with over 220 stores in four southeastern Brazilian states as of 2025.

companies.name: Havan
companies.description: Havan is a Brazilian department store chain headquartered in Brusque, Santa Catarina.

companies.name: Ferrous Resources
companies.description: Ferrous Resources Ltda. is a Brazilian mining company involved in the research, exploration, exploitation, processing, and marketing of iron ore. It operates within Brazil's mining sector.

companies.name: Petroleo Ipiranga
companies.description: Ipiranga Produtos de Petróleo S.A, known as Ipiranga, is a Brazilian fuel company headquartered in Rio de Janeiro. It is the second-largest fuel distribution company in Brazil and the largest in the private sector.

companies.name: Aeroalcool
companies.description: Aeroálcool is a Brazilian aerospace company based in Franca, São Paulo. It operates in the aerospace industry within Brazil.

companies.name: Flyer Indústria Aeronáutica
companies.description: Flyer Indústria Aeronáutica, Ltda. is a Brazilian manufacturer of light aircraft headquartered in Sumaré, São Paulo. It is part of Brazil's aerospace industry.

companies.name: Ultragaz
companies.description: Ultragaz is a Brazilian company that distributes liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). It originated from Empresa Brasileira de Gás a Domicílio, founded by Ernesto Igel, the founder of Ultra Group.

companies.name: Sodimac
companies.description: Sodimac Homecenter is a Chilean chain of home improvement stores with locations in several countries including Brazil. It operates in the commerce sector.

companies.name: Grupo RBS
companies.description: Grupo RBS is a Brazilian media conglomerate founded in 1957. It is one of Brazil's largest communication groups and the largest affiliated with TV Globo, comprising radio, television, newspapers, and online news portals.

companies.name: Linx (software house)
companies.description: Linx S.A. is a Brazilian management software company and the largest software house in retail management systems in Latin America. It holds a significant market share in Brazil's retail management software sector.

companies.name: KaBuM!
companies.description: KaBuM! is a Brazilian e-commerce company specializing in electronics and information technology. Founded in Limeira, São Paulo, it sells a wide variety of products including automotive electronics, cosmetics, and musical instruments.

companies.name: Prológica
companies.wiki: Prológica Indústria e Comércio de Microcomputadores
companies.description: Prológica Indústria e Comércio de Microcomputadores was a Brazilian microcomputer company influential in the mid-1980s. It ranked third among national companies in the computer industry sector at its peak.

companies.name: Teatro Oficina Uzyna Uzona
companies.description: Teatro Oficina Uzyna Uzona, commonly known as Teatro Oficina, is a theater company based in the Bixiga neighborhood of São Paulo, Brazil. Founded in 1958 at the University of São Paulo's Law School, it was established by Amir Haddad, José Celso Martinez Correa, Carlos Queiroz Telles, and Ron Daniels.

companies.name: Wet 'n Wild
companies.description: Wet ‘n Wild is a name used by various water parks operating in the United States, Brazil, and formerly Mexico. These parks were part of a water park chain originally owned by George Millay, the creator of SeaWorld. The brand is distinct from other similarly named water parks owned by different companies.

companies.name: Andrade Gutierrez
companies.description: Andrade Gutierrez is a private multinational conglomerate headquartered in Belo Horizonte, Brazil. Founded in 1948 by the Andrade and Gutierrez families, it is the second largest construction company in Brazil with over a thousand projects completed domestically and internationally. The company has branches in 44 countries.

companies.name: Neobus
companies.description: Neobus is the tradename of Brazilian bus manufacturer San Marino Ônibus e Implementos Ltda, based in Caxias do Sul, Rio Grande do Sul. Since starting production in 1996, Neobus has manufactured over 30,000 vehicles including microbuses, intercity, and touring coaches. Its primary manufacturing plant is located in Caxias do Sul.

companies.name: Renault do Brasil
companies.description: Renault Geely do Brasil, formerly Renault do Brasil, is the Brazilian subsidiary of French car manufacturer Renault and Chinese manufacturer Geely. Established in 1997, it is Brazil's fifth largest automaker by sales. In 2012, Brazil was the second largest market for Renault.

companies.name: Hyundai Motor Brasil
companies.description: Hyundai Motor Brasil is the Brazilian subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Company, located in Piracicaba, São Paulo. It is the first Hyundai plant in Latin America, completed in November 2012 with an investment of around R$1.2 billion. The plant has the capacity to produce 180,000 cars per year and includes complete vehicle production facilities.

companies.name: TV Bahia
companies.description: TV Bahia is a television station in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil, affiliated with TV Globo. It is the flagship station of Rede Bahia de Televisão, a statewide network of six stations. TV Bahia's studios and transmitter are located in Salvador, and its signal reaches 133 cities in the state.

companies.name: TV Oeste
companies.description: TV Oeste is a television station licensed to Barreiras, Bahia, Brazil, affiliated with TV Globo. Owned by Rede Bahia, it is part of Rede Bahia de Televisão, a statewide network of six stations. TV Oeste's studios are in Barreiras, and its transmitter is located atop Serra da Bandeira.

companies.name: TV Subaé
companies.description: TV Subaé is a television station licensed to Feira de Santana, Bahia, Brazil, affiliated with TV Globo. Owned by Grupo Modesto Cerqueira and Rede Bahia, it is part of Rede Bahia de Televisão, a statewide network of six stations. Its studios and transmitter are located in the center of Feira de Santana.

companies.name: Cutrale
companies.description: Sucocitrico Cutrale is a Brazilian company based in Araraquara, São Paulo, that produces oranges, orange juice, and orange by-products. Founded in 1967 by José Cutrale Jr., the company remains controlled by the Cutrale family.

companies.name: HSBC Bank Brasil S.A. - Banco Múltiplo
companies.description: HSBC Bank Brasil S.A. is a Brazilian subsidiary of the British banking group HSBC. It sold its retail banking operations in 2016 but returned in 2019 as a corporate bank, now operating exclusively as a wholesale bank providing services to companies in Brazil.

companies.name: Paris Filmes
companies.description: Paris Filmes is a Brazilian company involved in film distribution and production. It distributes movies in cinemas as well as on DVD and Blu-ray formats within Brazil.

companies.name: Easy Taxi
companies.description: Easy Taxi was a mobile app founded in Brazil in 2011 for taxi hailing, available in 30 countries. It allowed users to book and track taxis in real time and later became part of Cabify under Maxi Mobility group.

companies.name: Cinédia
companies.description: Cinédia was a Brazilian film studio established in Rio de Janeiro in 1930. It operated continuously until 1951, contributing to the Brazilian film industry during that period.

companies.name: Agência Estado
companies.description: Agência Estado is a private news agency in Brazil started by the Brazilian media group Grupo Estado. It operates within the Brazilian media landscape providing news services.

companies.name: Copersucar
companies.description: Copersucar is the world's largest sugar and ethanol company based in Brazil. It operates numerous mills across several states and is a major exporter and trader of sugar and ethanol globally.

companies.name: Tramontina
companies.description: Tramontina is a family-run metallurgical company founded in 1911 and headquartered in Carlos Barbosa, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. It operates in the metal goods industry.

companies.name: Grupo Bloch
companies.description: Grupo Bloch was a Brazilian media conglomerate founded by the Bloch family after arriving in Rio de Janeiro in 1922. It published pamphlets, magazines, and launched Manchete magazine in 1953.

companies.name: Grupo ND
companies.description: Grupo ND is a Brazilian media conglomerate headquartered in Florianópolis, Santa Catarina. Founded in 2019 after splitting from Grupo RIC, it includes a newspaper, seven TV stations, three radio stations, and a website.

companies.name: GGB Bearing Technology
companies.description: GGB Bearing Technology manufactures self-lubricating and prelubricated plain bearings and tribological polymer coatings. It has production facilities in multiple countries including Brazil.

companies.name: Avibras
companies.description: Avibras Aeroco is a Brazilian aerospace and defense company producing artillery, aircraft defense systems, rockets, missiles, and armored vehicles. It also manufactures civilian transportation and telecommunications equipment. The company is based in Brazil.

companies.name: Aeromot
companies.description: Aeromot Aeronaves e Motores S.A is a Brazilian industrial group marketing aeronautical products. It was responsible for the aeronautical system of the 2014 World Cup and 2016 Summer Olympics. The company is based at Salgado Filho Airport in Porto Alegre, Brazil.

companies.name: Seara Foods
companies.description: Seara Foods Ltda. is a Brazilian food processing company specializing in meat products. It was founded in 1956 in the town of Seara, Santa Catarina, Brazil.

companies.name: Companhia Brasileira de Cartuchos
companies.description: Companhia Brasileira de Cartuchos (CBC) is a Brazilian ammunition and weapons manufacturer. The company is based in Ribeirão Pires, São Paulo, Brazil.

companies.name: Elo
companies.description: Elo is a Brazilian national financial services corporation headquartered in Barueri, São Paulo. Founded in 2011, it was created by a holding company formed by Banco Bradesco, Banco do Brasil, and Caixa Econômica Federal.

companies.name: Industry Federation of the State of Rio de Janeiro
companies.wiki: Industry Federation of the State of Rio de Janeiro
companies.description: The Industry Federation of the State of Rio de Janeiro (FIRJAN) is a Brazilian industrial federation representing industries in Rio de Janeiro. It promotes debates, research, and projects for sustainable development and provides services to affiliated companies.

companies.name: Brazilian Red Cross
companies.description: The Brazilian Red Cross was founded in 1908 and has its headquarters in Brasília. It operates as a humanitarian organization in Brazil.

companies.name: Banco Real
companies.description: Banco Real was a Brazilian bank acquired by Spain's Banco Santander after a consortium led by Royal Bank of Scotland acquired ABN AMRO. Banco Santander integrated Banco Real with its Brazilian operations to become a major private bank in Brazil.

companies.name: Banco Safra
companies.description: Banco Safra is a Brazilian financial services company headquartered in São Paulo. It is the seventh largest banking institution in Brazil and the nineteenth largest in Latin America. The bank offers investment banking, private banking, asset management, and retail banking through its neobank AgZero.

companies.name: Grupo Silvio Santos
companies.description: Grupo Silvio Santos is a Brazilian holding company founded by the billionaire media-man Silvio Santos. It operates as a conglomerate in Brazil.

companies.name: Transpetro
companies.description: Transpetro, officially Petrobras Transporte S.A., is the largest oil and gas transportation company in Brazil. It manages a network of over 11,000 kilometers of pipelines and operates a fleet of various tankers for oil, gas, and biofuels transportation.

companies.name: Garoto
companies.description: Chocolates Garoto S.A. is a Brazilian chocolate and confectionery company headquartered in Vila Velha, Espírito Santo. Founded in 1929 by Heinrich Meyerfreund, it was acquired by Nestlé in 2002.

companies.name: Lacta
companies.description: Lacta is a Brazilian chocolate and confectionery maker founded in São Paulo in 1912. It was purchased by Philip Morris in 1996 and integrated into its Kraft Foods Division.

companies.name: Centro de Tecnologia Canavieira
companies.description: Centro de Tecnologia Canavieira (CTC) is the largest sugarcane technology center in the world, headquartered in Piracicaba, São Paulo. Founded in 1969, it serves sugarcane producers and processors across Brazil and is majority owned by Copersucar and Raízen.

companies.name: Amadeo Rossi S.A.
companies.description: Amadeo Rossi S.A. is a Brazilian firearms manufacturer founded in 1889 in São Leopoldo. It produces pistols and revolvers for civilians and security forces and exports worldwide, being one of Brazil's largest weapons manufacturers.

companies.name: EMGEPRON
companies.description: EMGEPRON is a Brazilian state-owned company linked to the Ministry of Defence through the Navy Command. It manages naval projects and commercializes Brazilian naval defense products and services.

companies.name: Estaleiro Atlântico Sul
companies.description: Estaleiro Atlântico Sul (EAS) is a Brazilian shipbuilding company founded in 2005 by Samsung Heavy Industries and Brazilian construction groups. Located in Suape port, Pernambuco, it features a large dry dock and uses shipbuilding technology supplied by Samsung.

companies.name: Estaleiro Mauá
companies.description: Mauá Shipyard SA is the oldest private Brazilian shipyard, originally founded as Estabelecimento de Fundição e Estaleiros da Ponta d'Areia. It was acquired in 1846 by Irineu Evangelista de Sousa, the Baron of Mauá.

companies.name: Lojas Riachuelo
companies.description: Lojas Riachuelo is a Brazilian department store company founded in 1947 in Natal, Brazil. The company operates 302 stores across the country. It is a notable retail chain in Brazil.

companies.name: Netshoes
companies.description: Netshoes is a Brazilian e-commerce sporting goods conglomerate established in 2000. It operates distribution centers in Brazil and manages official online stores for various soccer clubs and brands. It also represents the NBA in Latin America.

companies.name: National Beef Packing Company
companies.description: National Beef Packing Company LLC is a beef processor headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri, USA. Owned by Brazilian multinational Marfrig, it produces fresh and processed beef products worldwide. It is one of the major beef packers in the United States.

companies.name: Sky Brasil
companies.description: Sky Brasil is a subscription television service operator in Brazil owned by Vrio. The company produces TV content and owns several TV channels. It operates within the Brazilian telecommunications industry.

companies.name: Citrosuco
companies.description: Citrosuco is the largest global producer of orange juice concentrate, headquartered in Matão, Brazil. It holds significant market shares in Brazil and worldwide and is a subsidiary of the Votorantim Group. The company also produces orange by-products like essential oils and animal feed.

companies.name: Advanced Composites Solutions
companies.description: Advanced Composites Solutions (ACS) is a Brazilian engineering company specializing in composite materials technology. It focuses mainly on the development and construction of light aircraft. The company operates in the aerospace industry.

companies.name: H. Stern
companies.description: H. Stern is a Brazilian luxury jewellery house headquartered in Rio de Janeiro. Founded in 1945, it controls handmade jewellery production and operates over 150 stores worldwide. The company initially specialized in precious stones before focusing on design.

companies.name: Aperam South America
companies.description: Aperam South America is the largest Brazilian manufacturer of specialty steels, headquartered in Belo Horizonte. It supplies stainless, silicon, and special carbon steels and is the only stainless steel maker in Latin America. The company also mines iron ore.

companies.name: Agência Brasil
companies.description: Agência Brasil is a nationwide public news agency in Brazil, operated by the Brazilian government. Founded in 1990, it is part of the public media corporation Empresa Brasil de Comunicação, which was created in 2007 to unite two government media enterprises. The agency publishes content under the CC-BY license.

companies.name: Grupo Folha
companies.description: Grupo Folha is a Brazilian media conglomerate and the second largest in the country after Grupo Globo. It was founded by Octávio Frias and has been led by his son Luiz Frias since 1992. The company operates in the media industry in Brazil.

companies.name: IPE
companies.description: Indústria Paranaense de Estruturas Ltda, known as IPE Aeronaves, is an aircraft manufacturer based in Curitiba, Paraná, Brazil. The company specializes in producing gliders and general aviation aircraft. It operates within the aerospace industry.

companies.name: Conrad Editora
companies.description: Conrad Editora is a Brazilian book publishing company known for distributing manga and manhwa in Brazilian Portuguese. It operates within the publishing industry in Brazil.

companies.name: Editora Globo
companies.description: Editora Globo S.A. is a Brazilian publishing house owned by Fundação Roberto Marinho. It began as a bookstore called Livraria do Globo, founded in Porto Alegre in December 1883. The company operates in the publishing sector.

companies.name: Grupo Bandeirantes de Comunicação
companies.description: Grupo Bandeirantes de Comunicação is a Brazilian media conglomerate founded with the creation of Rádio Bandeirantes in 1937. Founded by João Saad, it has been chaired by his son Johnny Saad since 1999. The group operates in the media industry in Brazil.

companies.name: Algar Telecom
companies.description: Algar Telecom is a Brazilian telecommunications company operating in multiple states including Goiás, Minas Gerais, and São Paulo. It is the only operator that remained private after the creation of Telebrás and is the fifth largest in the telecommunications segment in Brazil.

companies.name: Sercomtel
companies.description: Sercomtel is a local phone and internet service provider in Paraná, Brazil. It offers landline, mobile, long distance phone services, and broadband internet. It was the only public telephone company in Brazil until its privatization in 2020.

companies.name: Baden Baden
companies.description: Baden Baden is a Brazilian microbrewery located in Campos do Jordão, São Paulo. Founded in 1999 as a model factory for craft beer production, it is now owned by Heineken. The company operates in the brewing industry.

companies.name: TAMAR Project
companies.description: The Projeto TAMAR is a Brazilian non-profit organization focused on protecting sea turtles from extinction along the Brazilian coastline. It is owned by the Chico Mendes Institute for Biodiversity Conservation and operates in the environmental sector.

companies.name: Colcci
companies.description: Colcci is a Brazilian fashion company specializing in clothing and accessories for men and women. It offers products such as jeans, t-shirts, dresses, skirts, and shoes. Colcci is one of the leading fashion brands in Brazil with a strong presence domestically and internationally.

companies.name: Alcântara Cyclone Space
companies.description: Alcântara Cyclone Space was a joint venture between Brazil and Ukraine established in 2006 to commercialize and launch satellites using the Ukrainian Cyclone-4 rocket from Brazil's Alcântara Launch Center. The cooperation was canceled by the Brazilian government in 2015.

companies.name: O Boticário
companies.description: O Boticário is a Brazilian cosmetics company operating 4,070 stores across Brazil and several other countries including Portugal, Mexico, and the United States. It is a major player in the cosmetics industry with an extensive international presence.

companies.name: Sistema Globo de Rádio
companies.description: Sistema Globo de Rádio is a Brazilian media group owned by Grupo Globo, originating with Rádio Globo in 1944. It controls several radio stations across Brazil and operates in the Pay-TV segment offering music programming to millions of subscribers.

companies.name: Federation of Industries of the State of São Paulo
companies.wiki: Federação das Indústrias do Estado de São Paulo
companies.description: The Federation of Industries of the State of São Paulo (FIESP) is a Brazilian industry entity affiliated with the National Industry Confederation (CNI). It represents industrial interests in the state of São Paulo.

companies.name: Internet Group do Brasil
companies.description: Internet Group do Brasil (iG) is a Brazilian internet service provider that operates web portals and offers services including news, shopping, and financial information. It provided free email accounts until 2016.

companies.name: Level Up! Games
companies.description: Level Up! Games is a game publishing studio originally from the Philippines, owned by Asiasoft since 2014. It operates in the Philippines and Latin America, focusing on the video game industry.

companies.name: Rei do Mate
companies.description: Rei do Mate is a Brazilian fast food chain specializing in tea house stores. It operates within the fast food restaurant industry in Brazil.

companies.name: Modern Logistics
companies.description: Modern Logistics, officially Modern Transporte Aéreo de Carga, is a Brazilian integrated cargo and logistics airline founded in 2014. It is headquartered in Jundiaí, São Paulo, and was founded by executives from Azul Linhas Aéreas.

companies.name: Aerosul Linhas Aéreas
companies.description: Aerosul Linhas Aéreas is a Brazilian airline based in Arapongas. It operates within the airline industry in Brazil.

companies.name: Placar Linhas Aéreas
companies.description: Placar Linhas Aéreas is a Brazilian non-scheduled passenger and cargo airline founded in 2022 and headquartered in São Paulo. It began operations in 2023, focusing on transporting football teams for matches within Brazil and other South American countries.

companies.name: Sol Linhas Aéreas
companies.description: Sol Linhas Aéreas Ltda. was a domestic airline based in Cascavel, Brazil. The summary does not provide further details about its operations or history.

companies.name: TAM Aviação Executiva
companies.description: TAM Aviação Executiva is a Brazilian airline specializing in air charter, aircraft sales, and maintenance. Founded in 1961 by Rolim Amaro, it remains owned by the Amaro family and is part of the TAM Group but not a subsidiary of TAM Airlines.

companies.name: Mais Linhas Aéreas
companies.description: Mais Linhas Aéreas S/A was an airline based in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, founded in 2010. It was authorized to operate domestic regular and non-regular flights.

companies.name: ASTA Linhas Aéreas
companies.description: ASTA Linhas Aéreas is a domestic airline based in Cuiabá, Brazil. Founded in 2009, it operates regular charter flights within the country.

companies.name: MAP Linhas Aéreas
companies.description: MAP Linhas Aéreas was a Brazilian domestic airline headquartered in Manaus, Amazonas. Founded in 2011, it operated regular and non-regular charter flights within Brazil and was the fifth largest airline in the country by domestic market share in 2023.

companies.name: Manaus Aerotáxi
companies.description: Manaus Aerotáxi is a non-scheduled airline and air taxi company headquartered in Manaus, Brazil. It specializes in charter flights and air medical services certified under Brazilian Civil Aviation Regulations.

companies.name: Total Linhas Aéreas
companies.description: Total Linhas Aéreas is an airline based in Brasília, Brazil, founded in 1988. It operates cargo and charter services and is among the largest domestic cargo airlines in Brazil by market share.

companies.name: Sideral Air Cargo
companies.description: Sideral Linhas Aéreas, formerly Sideral Air Cargo, is a Brazilian cargo and passenger charter airline headquartered in São José dos Pinhais, Paraná. It was established in 2009 as a subsidiary of Grupo Econômico Expresso Adorno.

companies.name: XP Investimentos
companies.description: XP Inc. is a Brazilian investment management company offering fixed income, equities, investment funds, private pension products, and wealth management services. It serves customers in Brazil and has offices in multiple international cities.

companies.name: Shalom Catholic Community
companies.description: The Shalom Catholic Community is an International Private Association of Faithful within the Catholic Church, founded in 1982 in Fortaleza, Brazil. It is affiliated with the Catholic Charismatic Renewal and operates in over 160 dioceses across more than 40 countries. Its headquarters are in Aquiraz, Ceará.

companies.name: Skymaster Airlines
companies.description: Skymaster Airlines was a cargo airline based in Manaus, Brazil. It operated charter cargo services within Brazil and other countries in the Americas. The airline specialized in cargo transportation.

companies.name: LATAM Brasil
companies.description: LATAM Airlines Brasil, formerly TAM Linhas Aéreas, is the Brazilian brand of the Chilean LATAM Airlines Group. It operates international and domestic flights from hubs in Brasília, Fortaleza, and São Paulo. It is the largest domestic and international airline in Brazil by market share.

companies.name: LATAM Cargo Brasil
companies.description: LATAM Cargo Brasil is a cargo airline based in Campinas, Brazil. It operates scheduled services within Latin America and between Brazil and the United States, as well as charter services. Its main base is Viracopos International Airport.

companies.name: Empresa Cubana de Aeropuertos y Servicios Aeroportuarios
companies.wiki: Empresa Cubana de Aeropuertos y Servicios Aeronáuticos
companies.description: Empresa Cubana de Aeropuertos y Servicios Aeronáuticos S.A. (ECASA) is a government-owned company operating 22 airports in Cuba, including José Martí International Airport in Havana. It manages airport operations across the country.

companies.name: CUPET
companies.description: CUPET is Cuba's largest oil company, owned and operated by the Cuban government. It is involved in petroleum extraction, refining, and distribution. Together with CIMEX, it operates a chain of filling stations selling gasoline in convertible pesos.

companies.name: Union de Industrias Militares
companies.description: The Unión de Industrias Militares is Cuba's state-owned military-industrial complex. It repairs weaponry and technology for the Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces and produces light weapons, ammunition, and other equipment. It also serves other requirements of the Cuban economy.

companies.name: ETECSA
companies.description: Empresa de Telecomunicaciones de Cuba S.A. (ETECSA) is the Cuban state company providing telephony and communications services. It holds a communications state monopoly and serves 8.2 million clients, both national and foreign.

companies.name: Aerogaviota
companies.description: Aerogaviota is a Cuban regional airline based in Havana. It operates domestic flights within Cuba and formerly served Jamaica. Its main base is Playa Baracoa Airport.

companies.name: Cubana de Aviación
companies.description: Cubana de Aviación is the flag carrier and largest airline of Cuba, founded in 1929. It has its headquarters in Havana and its home base at José Martí International Airport. The airline has been wholly owned by the Cuban government since 1959.

companies.name: Free Lives
companies.description: Free Lives is an independent video game developer based in Cape Town, South Africa. Founded in April 2012 and led by creative director Evan Greenwood, the company is known for creating the video game Broforce. It has also developed the comedy game Genital Jousting and the virtual reality game Gorn.

companies.name: StarSat
companies.description: StarSat was a South African direct broadcast satellite television service that began broadcasting on 1 May 2010. Operated by On Digital Media, it targeted middle class viewers and was partly owned by Luxembourgish satellite operator SES and Chinese company StarTimes. The service focused on the LSM 6-9 demographic.

companies.name: eNCA
companies.description: eNCA, also known as eNews Channel Africa, is a South African 24-hour television news broadcaster owned by Cape Town-based e.tv. Launched in June 2008, the channel focuses on African stories and events. It operates as a television news service within South Africa.

companies.name: Afrigen Biologics and Vaccines
companies.description: Afrigen Biologics and Vaccines is a South African biotechnology company based in Cape Town. The company operates within the biotech sector, focusing on biological and vaccine development. It is headquartered in Cape Town, South Africa.

companies.name: Tsogo Sun
companies.description: Tsogo Sun is a South African hotel, gambling, and entertainment group. It is half owned by Cape Town-based investment holding company Hosken Consolidated Investments. The company operates within the tourism industry in South Africa.

companies.name: Santam
companies.description: Santam is a South African financial services group focused on short-term insurance. Founded in 1918, it is headquartered in Bellville, Western Cape. Santam is listed on the JSE Limited and operates within the financial services sector.

companies.name: Africa Check
companies.description: Africa Check is a non-profit fact checking organisation established in 2012 to promote accuracy in public debate and media across Africa. It operates independently with offices in Johannesburg, Nairobi, Lagos, Dakar, and London, producing reports in English and French. The organisation tests claims made by public figures and institutions against available evidence.

companies.name: Denel
companies.description: Denel SOC Ltd is a South African state-owned aerospace and military technology conglomerate established in 1992. It is headquartered in Centurion, Gauteng. Denel operates within the aerospace and military technology sectors in South Africa.

companies.name: Spar
companies.description: The Spar Group Ltd, stylized as SPAR, is a major South African supermarket chain and the country's largest by total number of stores. Headquartered in uMhlanga, KwaZulu-Natal, it operates stores under the Dutch SPAR International brand in various countries. The company is traded on the JSE Limited.

companies.name: Takealot.com
companies.description: Takealot is a South African e-commerce company founded in 2011. It is owned by the major mass media corporation Naspers. The company operates within the e-commerce sector in South Africa.

companies.name: Wimpy
companies.description: Wimpy is a British fast-food casual dining chain that was founded in the United States. It found its success mainly in South Africa and has alternated between table-service and counter-service formats throughout its history.

companies.name: Steers
companies.description: Steers is a South African quick-service restaurant brand specializing in burgers and chips. Its menu also includes chicken burgers, ribs, ice cream, milkshakes, chicken, and salads.

companies.name: Dulce Café
companies.description: Dulce Café is a coffee shop and restaurant chain operating in South Africa. It originated in Port Elizabeth as a small ice cream shop in 1980 and has expanded to 53 stores across the country.

companies.name: Spur Corporation
companies.description: Spur Corporation Limited is a South African restaurant company operating several franchise chains including Casa Bella, Panarotti's, RocoMamas, and Spur Steak Ranches.

companies.name: Union Carriage & Wagon
companies.description: Union Carriage & Wagon (UCW) is a South African rolling stock manufacturer. In 2016, after Alstom acquired a majority stake, the company was renamed Alstom Ubunye.

companies.name: Protea Hotels
companies.description: Protea Hotels by Marriott is a South African hotel and leisure company headquartered in Cape Town. It was the largest hotel company on the African continent as of 2018, with 80 properties in ten countries.

companies.name: Hollywoodbets
companies.description: Hollywoodbets is a South African sports betting company offering a wide range of betting options including horse racing, football, cricket, rugby, and motorsport. It also offers over 2400 Lucky Numbers draws weekly and various gaming products.

companies.name: OK Bazaars
companies.description: OK Bazaars is one of South Africa's oldest retail shops, established in 1927. The first store opened in Johannesburg and the brand grew to more than 100 shops nationwide.

companies.name: South African Red Cross Society
companies.description: The South African Red Cross Society was founded in 1921 and has its headquarters in Johannesburg. It operates in emergency and relief services.

companies.name: Illovo Sugar
companies.description: Illovo Sugar South Africa is a sugar producer founded in 1891 and headquartered in uMhlanga, KwaZulu-Natal. It is a wholly-owned subsidiary of UK-based ABF Sugar and sources sugar cane from ten farms.

companies.name: Exxaro
companies.description: Exxaro Resources Limited is a South African diversified resources company that primarily produces coal. It operates within the mining industry and is based in South Africa.

companies.name: Kumba Iron Ore
companies.description: Kumba Iron Ore is an iron-ore mining company based in South Africa. It is notable for being the fifth largest iron-ore producer in the world and the largest in Africa.

companies.name: Public Investment Corporation
companies.description: The Public Investment Corporation (PIC) is a South African state-owned asset management firm headquartered in Pretoria, Gauteng. It is Africa's largest asset manager.

companies.name: Nando's
companies.description: Nando's is a South African multinational fast casual restaurant chain specializing in Portuguese flame-grilled, peri-peri style chicken. The name comes from a nickname for Fernando, one of the company's founders.

companies.name: Chicken Licken
companies.description: Chicken Licken is a South African fast-food fried chicken restaurant chain. It is recognized as the largest non-American-owned fried chicken franchise in the world.

companies.name: Massmart
companies.description: Massmart Holdings Limited is a South African retail company owning multiple major local chains such as Game, Makro, Builders Warehouse, and CBW. It is the second-largest distributor of consumer goods in Africa.

companies.name: Checkers
companies.description: Checkers is a South African supermarket retailer operating across Southern Africa. It is owned by Shoprite, a sister retailer and discount chain.

companies.name: Mugg & Bean
companies.description: Mugg & Bean is a full-service coffee-themed restaurant franchise founded in Cape Town, South Africa. It operates in the retail sector.

companies.name: Nedbank
companies.description: Nedbank Group is a South African financial services group offering wholesale and retail banking, insurance, asset management, and wealth management. Nedbank Limited is its wholly-owned subsidiary.

companies.name: South African Post Office
companies.description: The South African Post Office is the national postal service of South Africa and a state-owned enterprise. It is the oldest institution in South Africa, with origins dating back to 1792.

companies.name: Atlantis Diesel Engines
