companies.description: Megacable Holdings S. A. B. de C.V., known as Megacable Comunicaciones, is a Mexican cable operator providing internet and phone services. The company is headquartered in Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico.

companies.name: Paletería La Michoacana
companies.description: La Michoacana is a brand name used by several similar Mexican ice cream parlors. These are independent businesses that use the name but are not franchises, leading to variation in product quality, pricing, and assortment. The brand features pink branding and a Mexican woman in the logo.

companies.name: La Comer
companies.description: Grupo La Comer is a Mexican holding company of hypermarkets headquartered in Mexico City. It operates several hypermarket brands including La Comer, City Market, Fresko, and Sumesa. These stores have a strong presence in Mexico City and Central Mexico.

companies.name: Elektra
companies.description: Elektra is a Mexican retail chain founded in 1950 and part of Grupo Elektra. It operates nearly 1,300 locations across Mexico, Guatemala, and Honduras. The company sells household appliances, electronics, mobile phones, motorcycles, furniture, toys, and offers money transfer services.

companies.name: Las Estrellas
companies.description: Las Estrellas is a Mexican commercial broadcast television network owned by TelevisaUnivision. It began official broadcasts on March 21, 1951, and is distributed free-to-air across Mexico through affiliated stations. It is Mexico's most-watched television network and the nation's second-oldest television broadcaster.

companies.name: Grupo CIE
companies.description: Grupo CIE is a Mexican entertainment and media company leading the Latin American entertainment sector. It operates venues, auditoriums, and theme parks throughout Latin America and promotes live events, commercial fairs, and exhibitions. The company also operates ticketing sites including Ticketmaster Mexico and Ticketmaster Brazil.

companies.name: Grupo Reforma
companies.description: Grupo Reforma is the largest printed media company in Mexico and Latin America. It publishes ten daily newspapers in five cities, including leading newspapers in Mexico City, Monterrey, and Guadalajara. It also publishes the daily Metro in multiple cities and the afternoon tabloid El Sol in Monterrey.

companies.name: GT Global
companies.description: GT Global is one of the largest companies in northeastern Mexico, located in Tampico, Tamaulipas. Its main products include finance, automobiles, plastics, and tourism services. The company operates in multiple sectors within Mexico.

companies.name: Productos Mendoza
companies.description: Productos Mendoza, S.A. is a Mexican manufacturer of air guns, stationery, and firearms based in Mexico City. Founded in 1911 by Rafael Mendoza Blanco, the company initially produced firearms for troops under General Francisco Villa during the Mexican Revolution.

companies.name: Freightliner-Daimler México
companies.description: Freightliner-Daimler Vehículos Comerciales México is a manufacturer of trucks and tractors of American origin. Based in Mexico City, its first plant in Mexico opened in Saltillo, Coahuila on February 27, 2009.

companies.name: VUHL
companies.description: VUHL is a manufacturer of high performance automobiles headquartered in Mexico. The company was founded by brothers Guillermo and Iker Echeverria.

companies.name: Axtel
companies.description: Axtel S.A.B. de C.V. is a Mexican telecommunications company headquartered in San Pedro, near Monterrey. It offers telephone, internet, and television services through FTTH in 45 cities and provides IT services. It is the second largest landline telephone service provider in Mexico.

companies.name: La Parisina
companies.description: La Parisina is a chain of department stores in Mexico operated by Grupo Parisina S.A de C.V. It sells fabrics, millinery, home decor, embroidery, sewing machines, and rugs. The group began operations in 1933 and currently operates more than 600 stores across Mexico.

companies.name: Minera San Xavier
companies.description: Minera San Xavier was an open-pit mine in San Luis Potosí, Mexico, and a subsidiary of Canadian company New Gold Inc. It operated a gold and silver mine near Cerro de San Pedro. The mine is now closed after a lengthy closing process.

companies.name: Sears Mexico
companies.description: Sears Operadora México, S.A. de C.V. is a department store chain operating 93 stores across Mexico. It is operated by Grupo Sanborns, a division of Grupo Carso. The company is based in Mexico.

companies.name: Grupo Elektra
companies.description: Grupo Elektra is a Mexican financial and retail conglomerate founded in 1950. It operates over seven thousand points of contact across Mexico, the United States, and Central America through commercial and financial divisions. It is owned by Grupo Salinas.

companies.name: OXXO
companies.description: Oxxo is a Mexican chain of convenience stores and gas stations headquartered in Monterrey, Nuevo León. It operates over 21,000 stores across the Americas and parts of Europe. It is the largest chain of convenience stores in Latin America.

companies.name: Bodega Aurrera
companies.description: Bodega Aurrerá is a Mexican discount store chain and subsidiary of Walmart de México y Centroamérica. Founded in 1970 in Mexico City, it was originally part of Grupo Cifra before Walmart acquired majority control in 1997. The brand serves the discount market sector.

companies.name: El Palacio de Hierro
companies.description: El Palacio de Hierro is a Mexican upscale department store chain headquartered in Mexico City. As of 2025, it operates multiple department stores and freestanding stores for international brands. It is operated by Grupo Palacio de Hierro, part of Grupo BAL.

companies.name: Grupo Famsa
companies.description: Grupo Famsa is a Mexican retail company owning Famsa department stores. In 2023, it operated 21 stores and 21 personal loan branches in Texas. It was one of the most important retail stores in Mexico.

companies.name: Suburbia
companies.description: Suburbia is a Mexican chain of department stores founded in 1970 in Mexico City and now part of El Puerto de Liverpool group. It sells clothing, appliances, electronics, and cell phones targeting middle and lower economic classes. As of December 2023, it had 180 stores across Mexico.

companies.name: Unefón ICR
companies.description: AT&T Mexico, S.A.U. is a Mexican mobile telephone operator and subsidiary of AT&T. Headquartered in Mexico City, its network covers 90% of Mexico and serves 13% of the wireless market. It is the third-largest wireless carrier in Mexico.

companies.name: Señor Frog's
companies.description: Señor Frog's is a Mexican-themed franchised bar and grill located in tourist destinations throughout Mexico, the Caribbean, Tenerife, and the United States. It operates as a fast food restaurant chain.

companies.name: Softtek
companies.description: Softtek is a Mexico-based information technology company headquartered in Monterrey. It operates in North America, Latin America, Europe, and Asia, offering software development, testing, security, BPO, and IT infrastructure management. It is the largest private IT vendor in Latin America.

companies.name: Cámara Nacional de la Industria de Radio y Televisión
companies.wiki: Cámara Nacional de la Industria de Radio y Televisión
companies.description: The National Chamber of the Radio and Television Industry (CIRT) is the broadcasters' association of Mexico, representing all commercial broadcasters in the country. It is led by José Antonio García Herrera since 2021. The organization serves as a key industry association within Mexico's broadcasting sector.

companies.name: Squad
companies.description: Squad is a Mexican video game developer known for creating Kerbal Space Program, a space flight simulation game released in 2015. The game features realistic orbital physics and is available on multiple platforms including Linux, macOS, Windows, and consoles. Squad is based in Mexico.

companies.name: Badabun
companies.description: Badabun is a Mexican audiovisual production company that creates digital content primarily on YouTube. Founded in 2014, it gained popularity through humorous videos and internet celebrity collaborations. Badabun was recognized as the most popular Spanish-language channel on YouTube in 2019.

companies.name: Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide
companies.description: Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide, commonly known as AAA, is a Mexican professional wrestling promotion based in Mexico City. Founded as Asistencia, Asesoría y Administración de Espectáculos, it is known for its extensive touring schedule dubbed "La Caravana 3 Veces Estelar."

companies.name: Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre
companies.description: Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre is a Mexican professional wrestling promotion headquartered in Mexico City. Founded in 1933 as Empresa Mexicana de Lucha Libre by Salvador Lutteroth, it is the oldest professional wrestling promotion still in existence.

companies.name: Volkswagen de México
companies.description: Volkswagen de México is the Mexican subsidiary of Volkswagen Group, operating the group's plants and leasing and banking companies in Mexico. The company is headquartered in Puebla city and manages manufacturing and financial services related to Volkswagen in Mexico.

companies.name: Italika
companies.description: Italika is a Mexican motorcycle brand established in 2004 by Ricardo Salinas Pliego. It operates two assembly plants in Mexico and distributes motorcycles across Mexico, Guatemala, and Honduras. Italika is the top-selling motorcycle brand in Mexico with over eight million customers.

companies.name: Mercedes-Benz Mexico
companies.description: Mercedes-Benz Mexico is a subsidiary of the Mercedes-Benz Group, headquartered in Mexico City. It operates within the automotive industry in Mexico, representing the global Mercedes-Benz brand locally.

companies.name: Casas GEO
companies.description: Casas GEO was a leading housing developer in Mexico and one of the largest in Latin America. The company was involved in design, development, construction, marketing, sales, and delivery of mainly low-income housing across 52 cities in 16 Mexican states.

companies.name: Gamesa
companies.description: Gamesa is Mexico's largest manufacturer of cookies and also produces flour, ready-to-eat cereals, and related products. Headquartered in San Nicolás de los Garza, Nuevo León, it has production facilities in Mexico and Colombia. Gamesa was acquired by PepsiCo in 1990.

companies.name: Aeropuertos y Servicios Auxiliares
companies.description: Aeropuertos y Servicios Auxiliares (ASA) is a Mexican Federal Government-owned company headquartered in Mexico City. Established in 1965, it manages, operates, and develops Mexico's airports, operating 10 airports and part-operating 4 others, while also providing aviation fuel at 63 locations.

companies.name: Banco Azteca
companies.description: Banco Azteca is a financial institution headquartered in Mexico and part of Grupo Elektra and Grupo Salinas. Founded in 2002 by Ricardo Salinas Pliego, it focuses on promoting financial inclusion by serving middle and lower income groups often neglected by traditional banking.

companies.name: BanBajío
companies.description: Banco del Bajío, known as BanBajío, is a Mexican bank headquartered in León, Guanajuato. It is one of the major and fastest growing local banks in Mexico, ranking eighth in customer deposits and providing lending services.

companies.name: BanRegio
companies.description: Banregio Grupo Financiero, operating as BanRegio, is a Mexican regional bank headquartered in San Pedro Garza García near Monterrey. It offers financial services such as business loans, leasing, factoring, and working capital loans mainly to small and medium-sized companies.

companies.name: Bancomext
companies.description: Banco Nacional de Comercio Exterior (Bancomext) is a Mexican state-owned bank and export credit agency established in 1937. Its purpose is to promote foreign trade and support the export activities of Mexican companies.

companies.name: HSBC Mexico
companies.description: HSBC México, S.A. is the principal operating company of Grupo Financiero HSBC and one of Mexico's four largest banking and financial service companies. It has 1,400 branches and 5,200 ATMs and acquired Banco Internacional (Bital) in 2002.

companies.name: Ocean Star Cruises
companies.description: Ocean Star Cruises is a Mexican cruise line based in Mexico City, founded in 2010 as the first Mexican cruise line. Its first ship, Ocean Star Pacific, was purchased in 2010 and entered service in 2011.

companies.name: Cinépolis
companies.description: Cinépolis is a Mexico-based international movie theater chain and the largest cineplex chain in Mexico and Latin America. It operates 427 theaters in 97 cities and owns cinemas in several countries including Spain, India, and the United States.

companies.name: Sky México
companies.description: Sky México, a trading name of Corporacion Novavision, operates subscription television services in Mexico, Central America, and the Dominican Republic. Owned by Grupo Televisa, it produces TV content, owns several channels, and held a 59% market share in subscription TV as of 2022.

companies.name: Telcel
companies.description: Telcel, officially RadioMóvil Dipsa, S.A. de C.V., is a Mexican wireless telecommunications company owned by América Móvil. Founded in 1984 and based in Mexico City, it operates wireless networks across all nine geographic regions in Mexico using the 850 and 1900 megahertz radio spectrum.

companies.name: Altos Hornos de México
companies.description: Altos Hornos de México, S.A.B. de C.V. (AHMSA) is a steel plant located in Monclova, Coahuila, Mexico. It operates in the iron and steel industry and is situated approximately 155 miles from the United States border.

companies.name: Aeroméxico
companies.description: Aerovías de México, S.A. de C.V., operating as Aeroméxico, is the flag carrier airline of Mexico based in Mexico City. It operates scheduled flights to over 120 destinations across the Americas, the Caribbean, Europe, and Asia, with its main hub at Mexico City International Airport.

companies.name: Expansión
companies.description: Expansión is a Spanish-language business news magazine targeting markets in Mexico and Latin America. Created in 1969 and redesigned in 1999, it focuses on the people and ideas driving Mexico's private sector, distinguishing itself from other media that emphasize macroeconomic and political topics.

companies.name: Grupo Modelo
companies.description: Grupo Modelo is a large Mexican brewery owned by Anheuser-Busch InBev that exports beer worldwide. Its export brands include Corona, Modelo, and Pacífico, and it holds exclusive rights in Mexico for importing and distributing Anheuser-Busch beers.

companies.name: HEINEKEN Mexico
companies.description: Cervecería Cuauhtémoc Moctezuma is a major brewery based in Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico. Founded in 1890, it operates as a subsidiary of Heineken International.

companies.name: Librería Porrúa
companies.description: Librería Porrúa Hermanos y Compañía S.A. de C.V. is a longstanding bookseller and publishing company in Mexico. Known for its flagship bookstore in Mexico City and subsidiary stores nationwide, it has been associated with books and publishing since the early 20th century.

companies.name: Cinemex
companies.description: Cadena Mexicana de Exhibición S.A. de C.V., known as Cinemex, is a Mexican cinema chain operating multiplex theaters in multiple cities including Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Monterrey.

companies.name: Musart
companies.industry: Manufacturing and Reproducing Magnetic and Optical Media
companies.description: Discos Musart, or Musart Records, is a Mexican record label founded in 1948 in Mexico City and now headquartered in Miami, Florida. It produces, publishes, and distributes Latin music with a focus on regional Mexican genres, managing a large catalog of copyrights and master recordings.

companies.name: Aeroméxico Connect
companies.description: Aeroméxico Connect, formerly Aerolitoral, is a regional airline subsidiary of Aeroméxico based in Monterrey, Mexico. It operates Embraer 190 aircraft and provides feeder services to Aeroméxico's hubs with over 300 daily flights to destinations in Mexico, the US, Central America, and the Caribbean.

companies.name: Avianca Cargo México
companies.description: Avianca Cargo México, formerly AeroUnion, is a scheduled cargo airline headquartered at Mexico City International Airport. It operates cargo services within Mexico and between Mexico and the United States.

companies.name: Viva
companies.description: Viva, officially Aeroenlaces Nacionales, is a major Mexican low-cost airline headquartered at Monterrey International Airport. It is Mexico's third-largest airline by passenger numbers and serves over 50 destinations across Mexico, the US, Central, and South America.

companies.name: MasAir Cargo Mexico
companies.description: MasAir Cargo Mexico is a Mexican cargo airline based in Mexico City specializing in wide-body aircraft transport. It operates scheduled and charter services across the Americas, Asia, and Europe from its main hub at Felipe Ángeles International Airport and secondary hubs in Los Angeles and Zaragoza.

companies.name: Magnicharters
companies.description: Magnicharters, operated by Grupo Aereo Monterrey, was an airline headquartered in Mexico City. It operated domestic holiday flights out of Mexico City International Airport.

companies.name: Compartamos Banco ICR
companies.description: Compartamos Banco is a Mexican bank headquartered in Mexico City and the largest microfinance bank in Latin America. Founded in 1990, it serves more than 2.5 million clients.

companies.name: Aerodavinci
companies.description: Aerodavinci, officially Aero DaVinci Internacional, is an airline based in Reynosa, Tamaulipas, Mexico. Operating since 1997, it provides air taxi, cargo, and charter services.

companies.name: Avioquintana
companies.description: Avioquintana, or Aviones de Renta de Quintana Roo, is an air taxi service based in Quintana Roo, Mexico. Established in 1997, it operates domestic private charter services with its main base at Cancún International Airport and a hub at Chetumal International Airport.

companies.name: Estafeta Carga Aérea
companies.description: Estafeta Carga Aérea is a Mexican cargo airline based in Mexico City. It operates domestic cargo charters in Mexico and the US, with over 25 interline agreements connecting to the Americas, Europe, and Asia. Its main base is Ponciano Arriaga International Airport in San Luis Potosí.

companies.name: Aerolíneas Ejecutivas
companies.description: Aerolíneas Ejecutivas is an air charter operator founded in 1968 by Arturo Ortega Olive. As of 2015, it operated a fleet of 27 aircraft and flew approximately 15,000 hours per year.

companies.name: CALAFIAAIRLINES
companies.description: Calafia Airlines was a Mexican regional airline based in Cabo San Lucas, Baja California Sur. It operated regular and charter flights mainly within the Baja California Peninsula and Northern Mexico. The airline was named after Calafia, the legendary warrior queen of the island of California.

companies.name: Aéreo Servicio Guerrero
companies.description: Aéreo Servicio Guerrero is a Mexican regional airline founded in 1997. It is based at Hermosillo International Airport. The airline operates regional flights within Mexico.

companies.name: FlyMex
companies.description: FlyMex is a charter airline based in Toluca, Mexico. It operates under the legal name FlyMex, Servicios Integrales de Aviacion S.A. de C.V. The company provides aviation services primarily through charter flights.

companies.name: Regional Cargo
companies.description: Regionalcargo Holdings, operating as Regional Cargo, was a Mexican cargo airline. Its headquarters were located on the grounds of Querétaro International Airport and in Colón, Querétaro. The airline specialized in cargo transport.

companies.name: Republicair
companies.description: RepublicAir was a Mexican airline founded in 2004 and based at Toluca International Airport. It was banned from operations in April 2007 but resumed service in July 2007 with a single Boeing 737-200 aircraft. The airline operated passenger flights.

companies.name: MAYAir
companies.description: MAYAir is a regional airline based in Cancún, Quintana Roo, Mexico. Its main operational base is Mérida International Airport. The airline provides regional passenger air services.

companies.name: TAR México
companies.description: TAR México, legally Link Conexión Aérea, is a Mexican regional airline based in Querétaro. It operates scheduled flights to 12 national destinations using a fleet of Embraer ERJ 145 aircraft. The airline's main base is in Querétaro with additional focus cities.

companies.name: Aeronaves TSM
companies.description: Aeronaves TSM is a Mexican cargo charter airline headquartered in Saltillo. It operates from Saltillo Airport and specializes in cargo charter services. The company focuses on air freight transportation.

companies.name: Señor Air
companies.description: Cabo Flight Center, formerly known as Señor Air, is a Mexican regional carrier based at Cabo San Lucas International Airport. It launched scheduled operations on December 8, 2023, starting with one Embraer ERJ-135 aircraft. An Embraer ERJ-145 is expected to be added in 2024.

companies.name: Red Cross of Benin
companies.description: The Red Cross Society of Benin, also known as RCB, was founded in 1959. It is headquartered in Porto-Novo, Benin. The organization provides emergency and relief services.

companies.name: Royal Air
companies.description: Royal Air was a charter airline based in Cotonou, Benin, with its main base at Cadjehoun Airport. The airline ceased operations as of July 2012.

companies.name: COTAIR
companies.description: COTAIR was an airline based in Cotonou, Benin, established in 2008. It operated scheduled domestic flights and regional charter flights in West Africa, with its main base at Cotonou Cadjehoun Airport. The airline ceased operations on December 31, 2009.

companies.name: Mascom
companies.description: Mascom Wireless Proprietary Limited is a mobile telecommunications company headquartered in Gaborone, Botswana. It was established on February 17, 1998.

companies.name: BotswanaPost
companies.description: BotswanaPost is the company responsible for postal services in Botswana. It is a government-owned parastatal under the Ministry of Transport and Communications.

companies.name: Botswana Red Cross Society
companies.description: The Botswana Red Cross Society, also known as LRC, was founded in 1968 and is headquartered in Gaborone, Botswana.

companies.name: Air Botswana
companies.description: Air Botswana Corporation is the state-owned national flag carrier of Botswana, headquartered in Gaborone. It operates scheduled domestic and regional flights from Sir Seretse Khama International Airport.

companies.name: Wilderness Air
companies.description: Wilderness Air, formerly Sefofane Air Charter, is an air charter company headquartered in Botswana. It operates scheduled and charter flights, cargo operations, and runs a charity called Children in the Wilderness. It also operates Botswana's first flight simulator for pilot training.

companies.name: Mack Air
companies.description: Mack Air is a charter airline based in Maun, Botswana, operating in northern Botswana since 1994.

companies.name: Burkinabé Red Cross Society
companies.description: The Burkinabé Red Cross Society was founded in 1961 and is headquartered in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.

companies.name: La Poste Burkina Faso
companies.description: La Poste Burkina Faso, formerly SONAPOST until 2018, is responsible for postal services in Burkina Faso. Established in 1997, it succeeded the former National Post Office and Burkina Faso is a member of the West African Postal Conference.

companies.name: Air Burkina
companies.description: Air Burkina SA is the national airline of Burkina Faso, operating scheduled domestic and regional international flights from its main base at Ouagadougou Airport. The airline was majority owned by an AKFED/IPS consortium from 2001 to 2017 but is now back in government ownership. It serves destinations in several West African countries.

companies.name: Régie Nationale des Postes
companies.description: Régie Nationale des Postes is the company responsible for providing postal services in Burundi. It operates as the national postal service provider in the country.

companies.name: Burundi Red Cross
companies.description: Burundi Red Cross, founded in 1963, is a humanitarian organization based in Bujumbura, Burundi. It was established based on the Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols. The organization provides emergency and relief services in the country.

companies.name: Comoros Red Crescent
companies.description: The Comoros Red Crescent Society was founded in 1982 and recognized by the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement in 2005. Its headquarters is in Moroni, with regional branches on the Comoros islands. It manages relief supplies and has thousands of members and volunteers.

companies.name: Comores Aviation International
companies.description: Comores Aviation International was the flag carrier airline of the Comoros, operating domestic scheduled services and charters mainly to tourist destinations in southern and eastern Africa. Its main base was Prince Said Ibrahim International Airport in Moroni, with a hub at Ouani Airport.

companies.name: AB Aviation
companies.description: AB Aviation was a private regional airline and the largest in the Comoros, headquartered at Prince Said Ibrahim International Airport. The airline's air operator's certificate was revoked following a fatal accident in February 2022.

companies.name: Africanews
companies.description: Africanews is a 24/7 pan-African multilingual news network based in Lyon, France, previously headquartered in Pointe-Noire, Republic of the Congo. It began broadcasting online and via TV and satellite on 20 April 2016.

companies.name: Congolese Posts and Savings Company
companies.description: The Congolese Posts and Savings Company is a government-owned postal corporation in the Republic of Congo, created in 2001. It operates forty-eight post offices mainly in major cities, while many private companies also provide postal services, often without government permission.

companies.name: Trans Air Congo
companies.description: Trans Air Congo is an airline based at Pointe Noire Airport in Pointe-Noire, Republic of the Congo. The airline is banned from flying into European Union airspace.

companies.name: Equaflight
companies.description: Equaflight is an airline based in Pointe-Noire, Republic of the Congo, operating scheduled and charter flights from Pointe Noire Airport. Founded in 1998, it is a subsidiary of Regourd Aviation and is banned from entering the European Union since 2009.

companies.name: Gécamines
companies.description: Gécamines is a state-controlled commodity trading and mining company headquartered in Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Founded in 1966 as a successor to Union Minière du Haut-Katanga, it focuses on exploration, research, exploitation, and production of minerals including copper and cobalt.

companies.name: Trust Merchant Bank
companies.description: Trust Merchant Bank (TMB) is a commercial bank based in Lubumbashi, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Established in 2004, it operates across all local banking sectors including retail, SME, corporate, and mobile banking.

companies.name: Congolese Plantation Workers Art League
companies.description: The Congolese Plantation Workers Art League (CATPC) is an art cooperative founded in 2014 by plantation workers and environmental activist René Ngongo. It is based in Lusanga, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and built an art center named White Cube Lusanga in 2017.

companies.name: Supercell
companies.description: Supercell is a mobile phone network owned by Supercell SPRL operating in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

companies.name: Orange DRC
companies.description: Orange RDC is a telecommunications company operating in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with headquarters in Kinshasa. Originally a joint venture between ZTE and the Congolese state, it was fully acquired by France Télécom in 2011 and renamed Orange RDC in 2012.

companies.name: Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of Congo
companies.wiki: Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
companies.description: The Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of the Congo is the national Red Cross organization founded by the International Committee of the Red Cross. It joined the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in 1963 and is distinct from an earlier society that disbanded in 1909.

companies.name: Commercial Bank of Congo
companies.industry: financial service activities, except insurance and pension funding
companies.description: The Commercial Bank of Congo, formerly known as Banque du Congo Belge and later Banque Commerciale Du Congo (BCDC), operated in the Democratic Republic of the Congo from colonial times until 2020. It was acquired by Equity Group Holdings and became part of Equity Banque Commerciale du Congo.

companies.name: Air Kasaï
companies.description: Air Kasaï is an airline headquartered at N'Dolo Airport in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. It operates charter services within Africa with its main base at N'Dolo Airport.

companies.name: Flight Express
companies.description: Flight Express is an airline based in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. It operates charter services from its Kinshasa base.

companies.name: Compagnie Africaine d'Aviation
companies.description: Compagnie Africaine d'Aviation is a regional airline based in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Its main base is N'djili Airport in Kinshasa. The airline operates within the region.

companies.name: Filair
companies.description: Filair was an airline based in the Democratic Republic of the Congo operating from N'Dolo Airport in Kinshasa. It was banned by the European Union and Congolese authorities. The airline is no longer active.

companies.name: Air Tropiques
companies.description: Air Tropiques was an airline based in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. It operated domestic, regional, and charter flights from its main base at N'Dolo Airport. The airline is no longer active.

companies.name: Kivu Air
companies.description: Kivu Air is an airline based in Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo. It operates charter and cargo services with main bases at Goma International Airport and Bukavu Airport. The airline serves the local area.

companies.name: Great Lakes Business Company
companies.description: Great Lakes Business Company was an airline owner and operator in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The company was involved in the aviation industry within the country.

companies.name: Bracongo
companies.description: Bracongo is a brewery headquartered in Limete, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. It is part of Société des Brasseries et Glacières Internationales, which operates breweries across Africa. This group is owned by the French Groupe Castel.

companies.name: Bralima Brewery
companies.description: Bralima Brewery is a public limited liability company producing beer and soft beverages. It is headquartered on Avenue du Drapeau in Barumbu, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. The company operates in the beverage industry.

companies.name: Waltair
companies.description: Waltair was an airline operating in the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1983 to 2005. It was known for using the Sud Caravelle aircraft. Its operating certificate was revoked in 2005 and it was banned by the European Union.

companies.name: Free Airlines
companies.description: Free Airlines was an air operator based at N'Dolo Airport in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. It operated within the local aviation sector. The airline is no longer active.

companies.name: Karibu Airways
companies.description: Karibu Airways is an inactive airline based in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It was involved in the aviation industry but is no longer operational.

companies.name: MIBA Aviation
companies.description: MIBA Aviation was a cargo airline based in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Established in 1994, it operated Boeing 727 and Hawker Siddeley HS 125 aircraft. The airline ceased operations in 2005 after a Boeing 727 was written off.

companies.name: Djibouti Telecom
companies.description: Djibouti Telecom is the government-run telecommunications monopoly in Djibouti. It provides landline, mobile, and internet services, including 3G and 4G+ services. The company is headquartered in the national capital of Djibouti.

companies.name: Air Djibouti
companies.description: Air Djibouti, also known as Red Sea Airlines, is the flag carrier of Djibouti. It first operated in 1963, ceased operations in 2002, and was relaunched in 2015 with cargo and passenger services. The airline is headquartered in Djibouti city.

companies.name: Daallo Airlines
companies.description: Daallo Airlines is a Somali-owned airline based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It operates scheduled flights in the Horn of Africa and the Middle East. The airline is banned from flying in the European Union.

companies.name: Djibouti Air
companies.description: Djibouti Air was an airline based in Djibouti that operated between 2011 and 2012. Its logo featured the Djibouti spurfowl. The airline is no longer active.

companies.name: GEPetrol
companies.description: GEPetrol is the national oil company of Equatorial Guinea, founded in 2002 by presidential decree. It reports to the Ministry of Mines, Industry and Energy and is headquartered in Malabo. Teresa Isabel Nnang Avomo is the company's director.

companies.name: CEIBA Intercontinental
companies.description: CEIBA Intercontinental is an airline headquartered in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea. It is based at Malabo International Airport. The airline operates in the region from its main base.

companies.name: Ecuato Guineana
companies.description: Ecuato Guineana de Aviación (EGA) was Equatorial Guinea's national airline, established in 1986. It operated passenger and cargo services in West Africa from Malabo International Airport. The airline now appears to be defunct.

companies.name: Guinea Ecuatorial Airlines
companies.description: Guinea Equatorial Airlines (GEASA) is an airline based in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea. Established in 1996, it operates domestic charter services from Malabo International Airport.

companies.name: Cronos Airlines
companies.description: Cronos Airlines is a regional airline headquartered in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea. It operates passenger and cargo services within Equatorial Guinea and to Cameroon, Benin, and Nigeria. The airline is banned from flying in the European Union.

companies.name: Segesa
companies.description: SEGESA is the national electricity company of Equatorial Guinea, headquartered in Malabo. It is the sole operator of the country's electricity sector and was formed in 2001 by merging two national companies. In 2013, it reorganized into three units for distribution, generation, and transmission, overseen by SEGESA Holding.

companies.name: Punto Azul
companies.description: Punto Azul is a regional airline based in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea, with its main hub at Malabo International Airport. The airline operates scheduled flights mainly from Malabo, as well as private charters for the oil and gas industry and cargo services.

companies.name: Air Annobón
companies.description: Air Annobón was an Equatoguinean airline that began operations in January 2013 with flights between Malabo and Bata. It initially operated wet leased aircraft and later purchased its own plane. The airline suspended operations in September 2016 after failing to find a joint venture partner to resume flights as a low-cost carrier.

companies.name: Asmara Brewery
companies.description: Asmara Brewery is a brewery in Eritrea founded in 1938. It was nationalized during the Eritrean War of Independence and operates a football team competing in the Eritrean Premier League. The brewery employs over 600 people.

companies.name: EriTel
companies.description: EriTel, officially the Eritrean Telecommunication Services Corporation, is the sole operator of landline and mobile telephone services in Eritrea. It is one of several internet service providers in the country.

companies.name: Eritrean Airlines
companies.description: Eritrean Airlines is the national airline of Eritrea, based at Asmara International Airport and wholly owned by the government. It has been banned from flying into the European Union since December 2012 and is operationally defunct as of September 2024.
